title: 3D printing
examples: What is the difference between 3D printing and carving?
What kinds of things can you print with a 3D printer?
How does the printer know where to put the material?

explain.say: Today we are learning about three dimensional printing.
The process works by building objects layer by layer.
Printers use many different types of materials to build things.
These printed objects are used in many different real-life areas.
Think about making a custom phone stand for your desk.
A common mistake is thinking it prints all at once.

faq.a: No, it usually uses melted plastic or other solid materials. It is more like building with very precise glue.
asks: Is it like drawing with plastic?

faq.q: Can it print metal objects that are strong?
faq.a: Yes, some advanced printers can use metal powders to create very strong parts. These parts can be used in engineering.

faq.q: What is the role of the computer in this process?
faq.a: The computer creates the digital file that tells the printer exactly what to build. This file is called a model.
asks: Does the computer do the printing?
What file does the printer need?

faq.q: Is this process slow for big items?
faq.a: It can take a long time for very large or very detailed items. The printing speed depends on the object's complexity.
asks: Does it take a long time?

faq.q: Can I print things that are alive, like food?
faq.a: Some specialized printers can print food, but standard engineering printers use plastics and metals. Food printing is a different field.

facts: 3D printing is also called additive manufacturing.
It builds objects by depositing material in successive layers.
Materials can include plastics, metals, and resins.
It is used to create prototypes for real-world products.

quiz.say: If you are printing a toy car, what is the fundamental method used to build its shape?

options.show: Carving it out of a block
options.say: Carving it out of a block

quiz.why: The process adds material in thin, stacked sheets, which is the definition of layer by layer printing.

wrong.0: Molding involves pouring material into a space, not building up in steps.
wrong.1: The printer must build the object sequentially, not instantly.
wrong.3: Carving removes material, while 3D printing adds material.

quiz.say: Which material is often used for creating strong, custom parts for cars?
quiz.why: Metal powders can be fused layer by layer to create strong, durable components.

wrong.0: Wood composites are great for models but lack the required engineering strength.
wrong.2: While plastic is common, metal is needed for high-strength car parts.
wrong.3: Resin is often used for detail, but metal offers better structural strength for cars.

quiz.say: If a student wants to make a model of a human heart, which area of use is most appropriate?
quiz.why: 3D printing is vital in medicine for creating anatomical models for surgeons to practice on.

wrong.0: Toy making is too general; medicine points to a specific, high-tech application.
wrong.1: Architecture uses it for large structures, but medical models are a more precise application.
wrong.3: While art uses it, the specific function of medical models is key here.
